title: Bend a copper tube to 90 degrees in a lever bender, allowing for springback
instruction: Bend the tube in the bender to the 90 degree mark on the card, judged with the lever fully relaxed, then take both grippers away.
context: Plumbers and pipefitters (O*NET 47-2152.00) bend copper tube to an angle by hand. It is hard because tubes that look alike spring back by different amounts, seen only when the lever is relaxed, and a bend cannot be undone: pull, relax, read, and pull again.
setup: Two YAM arms at the near edge of a table; positions are (x forward from the arm bases, y left) in cm, heights above the table. A lever tube bender, 0.4 kg, stands free on the bench on a dark plate 20 x 34, with nothing fixing it down; friction between plate and bench is 0.4 at rest and 0.3 sliding. Its form wheel, 7 across, is at (33, 0). A form handle runs left along y and a lever runs right, both 17 long, with red rubber grips, 5 up. A 6 mm copper tube, drawn 1 cm thick so that it reads from above, lies against the form wheel on its far side, in line along y, beside the handles. A white card on the plate, 25 across, is marked for the tube's angle: green at 0, a red band from 87 to 93, black ticks at 70, 80 and 96. Pulling the lever towards the arms bends the tube; a return spring of 0.6 N m per radian brings the lever back to its start line, in line with the form handle, when let go. Two tubes in the same colour, by seed, spring back 12 or 4 degrees.
scoring: Measured with the protractor card, a ruler and a photo. 1.0 when the tube lies in the red band, from 87 to 93 degrees; the lever tip is within 1.5 cm of its start line, in line with the form handle; and both grippers are 3 cm clear of both handles, all still for 1 s. 0.5 when the lever tip is within 1.5 cm of its start line and both grippers are clear, and the tube reads from 80 to under 87, or over 93 up to 96. 0.25 when the lever tip is within 1.5 cm of its start line and both grippers are clear, and the tube reads from 70 to under 80. 0 otherwise, or if the tube reads past 96 degrees, or the bender leaves the bench or tips over.
reset_notes: A bent tube is consumed: start each trial with a new one, in the temper of that seed, lying straight. Odd seeds spring back 4 degrees; even seeds, and no seed, spring back 12.
fidelity: Rigid-body physics at 240 Hz on GPU. The tube is not simulated as a material: its set angle is the largest lever angle less the springback, one way only, and it follows the lever down to that. The load is the lever's spring. A real trial uses a bought bender with an added torsion return spring, and two tempers of 6 mm copper, measured for their springback. Both arms: pulling with one spins the light bender, but pressing down on it with one arm was not tried.
